policy: Every normative v5 requirement must have at least one mapped example.

requirements.rule: Create the contract before substantive drafting.
Preserve explicit owner constraints verbatim in the contract.
Label inferred defaults as defaults rather than owner instructions.
Resolve large-document and template-fidelity modes explicitly.
Map each research question to planned evidence.
Write inclusion and exclusion criteria before broad synthesis.
Define evidence-based stopping criteria.
Record tool and access limits before relying on unavailable evidence.
Start research with explicit questions and scope.
Separate candidate-source discovery from source acceptance.
Stop research by evidence criteria rather than arbitrary source count.
Carry unresolved evidence gaps into limitations and QA.
Record a source class for every accepted source.
Prefer primary evidence for authoritative claims when feasible.
Assess freshness relative to the claim and domain.
Do not treat repeated secondary reporting as a substitute for primary support.
Validate bibliographic metadata appropriate to source type.
Never guess a DOI, URL, author, date, page or publisher field.
Deduplicate without merging distinct editions or versions.
Export CSL-JSON, BibTeX/BibLaTeX or RIS without inventing absent fields.
Assign a stable SRC identifier to every accepted source.
Record which claims each source actually supports.
Preserve source limitations and verification status.
Keep source identifiers stable across citations, visuals and QA artifacts.
Assign stable IDs to critical and major factual claims.
Map each supported claim to the exact supporting source proposition.
Preserve materially contradictory evidence.
Block clean release for unsupported critical claims unless explicitly treated as unresolved.
Normalize scope before declaring two sources contradictory.
Disclose material genuine conflicts.
Record evidence gaps and their impact.
Never fabricate consensus from incompatible evidence.
Select the document mode before outline generation.
Use section grammar appropriate to the selected mode.
Reserve labels such as systematic review for matching methodology.
Allow owner or journal rules to override generic mode defaults.
Generate structure from mode, audience and research question.
Give every major section a declared purpose.
Remove unjustified placeholder sections.
Keep heading hierarchy stable for navigation and chapter splitting.
Define the review question and inclusion boundary.
Group evidence by meaningful themes, methods, populations or explanations.
Do not accept serial one-source summaries as final synthesis.
Link gaps and contradictions back to evidence records.
Select and record one citation style.
Keep in-text citations or notes consistent with the bibliography style.
Use real Word notes when claiming note-based citations.
Never fabricate live citation-manager behavior.
Choose front matter from document type and submission rules.
Regenerate the abstract from the final content.
Use keywords that represent actual searchable concepts.
Never invent authorship, affiliation, funding, ORCID or compliance statements.
Keep mathematics semantically correct and editable where supported.
Define symbols and variables consistently.
Use stable equation numbering and references when needed.
Treat rasterized equations as a disclosed fallback, not the default.
Include only glossary terms actually used and needed.
Maintain one canonical expansion for each acronym.
Do not add unused glossary or index filler.
Claim dynamic Word indexing only when real fields are present and verified.
Prevent stranded headings and captions.
Use section breaks for orientation changes.
Repeat headers and manage continuation for long tables.
Verify page, chapter, appendix and equation numbering after final pagination.
Treat an authoritative supplied template as controlling.
Reuse existing semantic template styles before creating alternatives.
Do not substitute unauthorized brands or logos.
Document and visually verify unavoidable template deviations.
Obtain target submission rules from the identified publication.
Anonymize only when required and only on a derived copy.
Check word, figure and reference limits before release.
Report submission compliance as PASS, FAIL or UNVERIFIED.
Preserve the original before revision.
Track a disposition for every reviewer comment.
Verify native comments or Track Changes structurally when claimed.
Give a reasoned response to rejected reviewer requests.
Keep audit artifacts synchronized with the delivered document version.
Preserve stable source IDs across all audit artifacts.
Do not redistribute protected full-text source content without permission.
State exactly what was verified and what remains unverified.
Normalize terminology or document intentional variants.
Flag duplicated substantive passages.
Resolve or disclose contradictory internal statements.
Preserve meaning and evidence support when applying consistency fixes.
Quote or genuinely paraphrase distinctive borrowed wording.
Preserve attribution after paraphrase.
Keep direct quotations exact and located when available.
Never fabricate plagiarism or AI-detector scores.
Choose table or figure type from the information shape.
Retain source data, units and provenance for quantitative visuals.
Route oversized tables to landscape, appendix or a justified split.
Keep captions, numbering and cross-references stable after edits.
Calculate dashboard counts from machine-readable ledgers.
Separate blocking failures from informational warnings.
Do not invent a composite quality score without a defined validated model.
Reflect unresolved blockers in final release status.
Execute dependent stages in the required order.
Use stable IDs and machine-readable handoff artifacts where defined.
Route blocking defects back to the stage that owns them.
Report verified and unverified stages explicitly at release.
Add a visual only when it produces a real comprehension gain.
Choose visual type deterministically from the reader task and information shape.
Require provenance, rights, caption, alt text and legibility for factual visuals.
Inspect the final rendered page and remove redundant or defective visuals.
Use real Word styles and fields rather than visually faked equivalents.
Use real PAGE/TOC/SEQ/REF/STYLEREF features only when actually present.
Keep textual content editable instead of rasterizing whole pages.
Disclose unsupported native Word features instead of pretending they were created.
Preserve semantic headings, table headers, reading order and meaningful alt text.
Apply real RTL/bidi behavior for Arabic rather than right alignment only.
Perform independent language-specific proofreading and terminology QA.
Do not encode essential meaning by color alone.
Assign a stable REQ ID to every v5 normative rule.
Map every REQ ID to at least one example.
Give each example a scenario, correct path, incorrect path and acceptance evidence.
Require 100 percent example coverage before release.
Default estimated or rendered documents of 100 pages or more to Chapter Package Mode unless overridden.
List every chapter exactly once in both manifest and Index.
Use relative external hyperlinks from the Word Index to chapter DOCX files when possible.
Run independent chapter QA plus package-level consistency QA.
Make package contents match the Document Contract.
Verify that every claimed artifact exists and validates where tooling allows.
State verified and unverified status explicitly.
Include Index, manifest and every declared chapter file in Chapter Package Mode.
